newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares close a shade up in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close a shade up in cautious trade.

text.p: Manila shares end slightly up on Monday after see-saw trading as the market continues to look for fresh incentives to spur buying, traders said.
"The market was sluggish because a lack of fresh news weighed down the market," said Poch Zamora, a dealer at Peregrine Securities.
Value turnover was thin at 3.0 billion pesos compared to the previous 3.5 to 4.0 billion worth of daily transactions.

"The market was mostly sideways and that is unusual because of PLDT's big rise in New York. There is probably still an overhang from the Victorias debacle," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.
Garcia was referring to news that sugar miller Victorias Milling Co was able to secure last week a moratorium for its $167 million loans from several local banks.
Traders said the market did not react much to the Dow Jones' climb to the 7,000 level last Friday or to PLDT's American Depositary Receipt (ADR) rise by $1-3/4.
Some investor interest was dampened by the internal squabbles at the stock exchange which led to the resignation of Philippine Stock Exchange president Vitaliano Nanagas on Saturday, traders said.
In the broad market, gainers slightly outnumbered losers 54 to 51 with 92 issues unchanged.
Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities, said that the initial public offering of Equitable Bank which started last week are also keeping investors at bay from fundamentally-sound stocks.
"I think we will see more of the same tommorrow up to the end of the month until we have more significant developments in the corporate front," said Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Securities.
